note: Everything a storyboard (film/shots.json) may reference. The director and pipeline/storyboard.py both read this file.

roles.commoner: ordinary person in a plain tunic or shirt and flat cap
roles.elder: older man in a grey robe
roles.noble: wealthy person in a white toga with a purple stripe and laurel wreath (Roman era)
roles.roman_soldier: Roman guard in a red tunic and crested helmet
roles.settler: frontier farmer in a cream shirt, suspenders, wide-brim hat, moustache
roles.red_soldier: British Royal Marine in red tunic and shako
roles.blue_soldier: US infantry in dark blue with a kepi
roles.official: man in a dark suit and top hat, moustache
roles.monarch: ruler in a dark military coat with gold epaulettes, silver hair, moustache

palace.desc: Roman palace hall: marble floor, columns with torches, red painted walls, a heavy curtained alcove on the back wall, a litter available as a prop

farm.desc: sunny potato field with fence, log cabin, pine forest and sea in the distance

camps.desc: grassy ridge with two facing military camps (tents, flags): blue (US) camp at +z and red (British) camp at -z, no-man's land between

pier.desc: wooden pier on a calm bay with a tall sailing ship moored at the end

props.curtain: palace only; {"open": 0..1 or [from,to], "sway": 0..1}. Actor placed at anchor 'curtain' stands hidden behind it with only the feet visible below the hem
props.litter: {"from":anchor|[x,z], "to":anchor|[x,z], "rider": cast id, "bearers": [cast ids]}: a carried platform that moves from..to over the shot

sizes.medium: waist up, a person or two

camera.extras: optional: "subject" (cast id | anchor | 'curtain'), "y" (world height in metres to aim at, e.g. 0.4 for feet), "roll" (small dutch tilt 0..0.1)

timing: t0 of each shot is 'L<n>' (start of narration line n), 'L<n>@<word>' (when that word is spoken; optional '#2' for the 2nd occurrence), or seconds. Shots must be listed in time order and the first starts at 0.

action_notes.hide: trembling, arms to chest; combine with anchor 'curtain' to be hidden behind it
action_notes.walk: moves from 'at' to 'to' over the shot (face defaults to travel direction)
